findings.reason: the missing s7→s5 edge changes the build order and lets a node be dispatched against a section that cannot supply one of its listed outputs.
findings.text: plan-section-depends-on gives s7 the dependencies s2, s3 and s4, but §7 (line 231) says it "composes, from §2 to §5" and its brief carries "wiring findings, counted, with the top three shown" (line 225), which are §5's undeclared-wait and overlapping-scope outputs; s5 is not an ancestor of s7, so a scheduler honouring the declared map can build §7 before §5 exists and the brief cannot produce those rows

findings.reason: §6 should split into sections so each deliverable carries its own reviewable verdict, as §2 to §5 each do.
findings.text: §6 bundles three separable deliverables — the slug@f-id ref grammar, the new `descoped` declaration, and the refusal text naming the keyed write path — and its done-when (line 204 onward) asserts three distinct behaviours, so the section can be neither reviewed nor closed on one verdict and its gate proves only whichever third ran

findings.reason: without a declared control or a known-wrong input, §8's measure cannot fail and so measures nothing about the derivations it exists to validate.
findings.text: §8's done-when turns on "Every disagreement with a coordinator is listed with its cause", an assertion that is satisfied vacuously when no disagreement is found, and the section declares no negative control, so a derivation that is wrong in a way no coordinator happens to notice passes the node's gate; §2 to §6 each declare an arm that must fail on the base commit and §8 declares none

findings.reason: the section's stated control cannot fail on the defect it exists to catch (a wrong leading figure), so §7 needs a declared failing arm on a fixture, as its siblings have.
findings.text: §7's control is a parity test, but §7 itself defines the brief as "a composition, not a second analyser: every figure in it is read from the brief's own payload", so the parity assertion holds by construction whenever the composition is faithful and can only catch a brief that re-derives, not a brief whose figures are wrong; no base arm is named

findings.reason: the plan's central causal claim is contradicted by the code it cites, and a builder reading §2 as "add propagation for these three edge kinds" would double-handle the gate and plan-level ones instead of extending the plan-section-depends-on path the base actually drops.
findings.text: §1 states the analyser "rolls everything up to plan granularity before computing paths, so the edges cancel out … a section-level edge between two plans never becomes an unlocks", but at the base revision reckon/roadmap.py:2955-2970 adds every cross-plan gate-section edge to `dependents` (hence to the target's `unlocks`) and roadmap.py:2878-2887 does the same for a section-qualified plan-level depends-on ref, so two of the three edge kinds §2 lists (line 78-81) already propagate to plan-level unlocks; the stated cause is broader than the cited evidence (the power_convertor table) supports and §2 will re-cover edges the base already handles

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2 to §6 each name a base-commit negative control, but §7's parity test is tautological by its own definition and §8 declares no control at all.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 and §5 write to "the gate log" and §8 to the cumulative landed record; no section names a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's stated root cause overstates what the base analyser does, and §2's edge list partly re-covers edges the base already propagates to plan-level unlocks.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §6 carries three independent schema deliverables (followup ref grammar, the `descoped` declaration, the refusal text) each with its own test.
